Subject: Activation runway & MAP ledger — proposed capacity tranche plan

Hi Elliot / Nadia —

Thanks again for yesterday's product walkthrough. Per our conversation I attached a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) draft and a GPU sizing worksheet that aligns evaluation milestones to capacity commitments. High level proposal: full Dedicated activation in three tranches (H100-equivalent): 12 -> 24 -> 36 GPUs tied to evaluation gates. Key constraints below:

- Lead times: procurement + provisioning for Dedicated Private pools: expected 14–18 weeks for initial tranche (varies by region).
- Hedge recommendation: reserve an initial tranche equal to your alpha-run peak (we suggest 12 GPUs) to avoid retraining delays while the evaluation completes.
- Acceptance gates: canary traffic (week 4), load validation (week 8), SLA sign-off (week 12).

Next steps I propose:
1) You review the MAP draft (RDW_MAP_Aurora_v1.3.pdf).
2) Procurement confirms internal approval timeline; we’ll align tranche dates with your fiscal commitments.
3) Redwood ops sizes the pool and issues a capacity PO draft.

I’ll loop in Ben and Marissa (ops & onboarding) so we can model the lead-time buffer into the MAP.

Best,
Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Strategic Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, reviewed the MAP and worksheet with the ML team. A few clarifying asks before procurement will sign:

1) Can you compress lead time for tranche 1? We need the alpha environment in 10 weeks if possible.
2) What are fallback options if the supplier delays hardware beyond 18 weeks?
3) Does Redwood support a mixed tranching model (H100 + 8-bit quant instances) to reduce initial cost while preserving throughput?

Procurement will aim to give an approval window by 07/08 but want to understand scheduling risk. Nadia asked to see a lane that hedges lead time risk (e.g., partial hosted capacity while Dedicated is provisioning).

—Elliot

Subject: Re: Activation runway & MAP ledger — internal sizing/lead-time options for Aurora

Folks — quick ops note after running the worksheet:

- Lead-time realistic range for Dedicated H100-equivalent nodes: 12–20 weeks depending on region and availability. The 10-week target is tight but potentially feasible with an expedited procurement and a partial-hosted bridge.
- Fallbacks: (a) temporary hosted capacity on Redwood Hosted API for latency-insensitive evals (we bill usage), (b) hybrid pool: dedicated CPUs + quantized GPUs for warm-up, (c) partner brokered capacity (higher cost).
- Sizing: alpha = 12 GPUs (sustained 40 RPS @ 1k context); beta = +12 (total 24); GA = +12 (total 36). Recommend reserve windows: tranche commits at T0 (12), T+8w (additional 12), T+16w (final 12).

I’ll prepare two MAP lanes for Kimberly to share:
1) Fast-track lane (aggressive PO + hosted bridge) — aims for ~10w first activation, higher total cost but lower schedule risk.
2) Conservative lane (standard provisioning) — 14–18w cadence, lower cost but longer wait.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Onboarding — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Activation runway & MAP ledger — options and recommended MAP lanes

Elliot / Nadia —

Following ops' modeling, attached are two MAP lanes in the updated MAP (v1.4):

- Fast-track lane: PO signed; Redwood provisions burst-hosted bridge (estimated 2–4 weeks to stand up) while we prioritize expedited hardware shipments. Expected first tranche in ~10 weeks from PO. Cost delta ~+28% for first 12-week period.
- Standard lane: no hosted bridge; Dedicated provisioning only. First tranche 14–18 weeks from PO. Lower immediate spend.

We'll capture the chosen lane, tranche dates, acceptance gates, and billing checkpoints in the MAP contract addendum. Please confirm which lane Procurement prefers and whether they can provide a target PO date. If useful, we can scope a formal SOW for the hosted bridge to accelerate evals.

Thanks,
Kimberly
